neutral_facts.value: The accused was alleged to have committed rape on a minor girl. The victim, who was 17 years old at the time of the incident, attempted suicide after the alleged rape and later disclosed the incident to her family and the police. The victim's family reported the case to the police, leading to the registration of an FIR. The victim underwent medical examination, and the medical report indicated that her hymen was intact. The accused was arrested and charged under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code. The trial court convicted the accused and sentenced him to seven years of rigorous imprisonment along with a fine of Rs. 5,000. The High Court upheld the conviction and sentence. The accused appealed, arguing that the delay in lodging the FIR and the medical evidence undermined the prosecution's case. The Supreme Court examined the evidence, including the victim's testimony, the delay in reporting the incident, and the trauma experienced by the victim. The Court found the prosecution's case credible, noting that the delay in reporting the incident and the victim's suicide attempt supported her account of the rape. The Court also emphasized that the amendment to Section 114-A of the Evidence Act supported the prosecution's case, even in the absence of clear medical evidence of rape.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the delay in lodging the FIR was fully established, the time gap between the incident and the FIR is a clinching evidence, and the prosecutrix's version of the incident was supported by circumstantial evidence and cross-examination. The medical evidence regarding the hymen was considered not significant due to the time gap between the incident and the examination.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the appellant was falsely implicated due to enmity, the delay in lodging the FIR was unexplained, the medical evidence showed the hymen was intact, and the prosecutrix's suicide attempt was due to examination fear rather than rape.

quotes.text: The appellant was falsely implicated due to enmity. It was further submitted that there was 20 days delay in lodging of the FIR; that the girl attempted suicide because of examination fear and that the medical evidence that the hymen of the victim was intact belied the prosecution case of rape

The defence no doubt has taken the plea that the girl had attempted suicide due to the examination fear and not on account of the rape alleged to have been committed on her but the same does not stand the test of scrutiny

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the offence of rape can be proved even if there is an attempt of rape and not the actual commission, and that the victim's version should be believed if supported by circumstantial evidence and other attendant circumstances.

quotes.text: In view of the amended s. 114-A of the Evidence Act, even if there had been a doubt about the medical evidence regarding non rupture of hymen, the same would be of no consequence as it is well settled that the offence of rape would be held to have been proved even if there is an attempt of rape on the woman and not the actual commission of rape
The prosecution version cannot be brushed aside totally and will have to be judged by the other attendant circumstances brought on record
